title: We're turning Alan Thrall into a bodybuilder!
summary: Recorded consultation where NH writes a one-year hypertrophy program live for strength coach Alan Thrall: a 5-day upper/lower/arms/upper/lower split built on supersets, choices between exercise rotations, double progression with a rep range, and strongman events picked for hypertrophy. It shows his whole process, from intake questions about weak points, frequency and equipment through to building the program in order of priority.
claims: Alan Thrall, 15+ years of strength sports, in his 30s, natural, business owner and new dad, will do a full year of hypertrophy training under his program
Strength athletes leave physique to chance; after his cut Alan realised his physique wasn't where he wanted
Typical strength programs tack isolation on at the end, where it gets skipped or done tired; that is not hypertrophy programming
Natural bodybuilding is mostly compounds plus isolation, but isolation is treated with the same priority and seriousness as compounds
Isolation-only bodybuilding programs are bad and lead to plateaus
Alan's weak points are arms and mid back; his legs are huge so leg volume and intensity can be lowered
Upper-body muscles never trained directly are effectively at a novice stage, so he could grow even at maintenance; a surplus will help
Alan's 5 days at 2 hours allow an upper/lower/arms/upper/lower split
In bodybuilding specificity is about the movement pattern: vertical pressing 2-3x a week rather than the same overhead press
For bodybuilding, about 6 reps is the lowest you should go and the upper end is usually 12-15; Alan will mostly work in 6-12
Bench and overhead press can be the meat and potatoes for chest and shoulders; claims they are suboptimal are overblown
Atlas stones and sandbags are a poor stimulus-to-fatigue way to train biceps: few reps, isometric only
Strongman biceps tears come partly from biceps never being trained through full range of motion
When adding isolation for someone new to it, start low volume with decent intensity, watch tendon response, and rotate variations if they get sore
Pain does not automatically mean danger
Pull-ups 1-2x a week with grip rotation is enough to progress well
Low-intensity running 2x a week for 20-30 min does not hurt gains; the idea that cardio kills gains or testosterone is a myth
Supersetting a horizontal press with a horizontal pull is his default pairing
Program days offer two exercise options each so an advanced lifter autoregulates by instinct
Neck training is superset with the first lower-body lift so it can't be skipped, 3x15-20; neck stays in higher reps for safety
Snatch-grip RDLs also stretch the traps and upper back
Russian twists and decline sit-ups with torso rotation target obliques and serratus; add weight as you get strong
Rear-delt and side-delt work (upright rows, rear-delt rows) stays at 10-15 reps to failure to protect the shoulder
Arm days should open with a heavy compound, not 20-rep curls and kickbacks
Dumbbell skull crushers are easier on the elbows than EZ because you can tuck the elbows; rotate to them if tendinitis appears
Long-head triceps fatigue faster than biceps, so use a lower rep range
Towel hammer curls through a plate are a much harder forearm variation
Stretch-position biceps exercises (pelican, spider curls) use higher reps, 10-15, for tendon longevity
Triceps take long to recover, especially if untrained, so the third long-head session is done only if fresh
Program both deadlifts and RDLs; deadlifts at low volume, high intensity: 1x5 or 3x3, or block pulls 3x6-12
Leg curls help prevent hamstring tears common in strongman
No RPE: isolation always goes to failure; squats and hinges stay at 1-2 RIR
Double progression: e.g. 3x6-10 goes 7/6/6, then 8/7/6, 9/8/7, until the top of the range is maxed, then add weight
Load is a tool to stay inside the rep range; if a jump drops you below it, you were too greedy
Keep each lift's rep range fixed so you can tell whether you are progressing
Flexibility in exercise choice day to day is a big plus of bodybuilding
exercises: Russian twist / decline sit-up with rotation
Hammer Strength high row / single-arm cable row diagonal
